grad_b1_global_rel_l2.coverage: full: every element of all 338 unique trainable tensors (1,543,714,304 elements)

loss_update1_max_rel.coverage: all 4 microbatch raw losses of update 1 (forward from the identical start)

dtheta_final.coverage: full: every element (fp32 master for DeepSpeed)

descriptive_only: dtheta_final relative L2 and per-tensor values
zero_denominator: a tensor whose reference norm is 0 gets no relative value (null) and is listed; global metrics use global norms; a zero global reference norm makes the metric 'missing' (never a pass)

consequences.graded metric pass / marginal / fail: recorded as the numerical finding; does not stop later independent cases

justification.source: the graded limits are the values pre-registered on 2026-10-14 (evidence: v2_validation_20261014a/evidence/analysis/numerical_reference_preregistration.md, hashed before any reference run), applied unchanged; they were not derived from any observed discrepancy
justification.bf16_compute: bf16 unit roundoff u = 2^-8 = 3.9e-3; each matmul output carries O(u) relative error; through ~28 transformer layers gradient errors of 1-3% are expected, so 0.05 (~13u) passes that while still catching normalisation mistakes (a missing 1/GA = 1/4 gives a relative error of 3; a skipped reduction or sign error >= 1)
justification.bf16_weights_and_accumulation: DeepSpeed bf16 keeps weights, activations, norms and residuals in bf16 and accumulates the 4 microbatch gradients in bf16 (live data_types bf16/bf16): more rounding steps than autocast, hence the looser 0.08 / 0.99 limits registered for bf16-weight recipes
justification.marginal: pass limit x 3 (or 1 - 3 x (1 - cosine limit)), as registered
justification.loss: forward-only quantity averaged over 1023 tokens; 5e-3 ~ u for bf16 compute, 1e-2 for bf16 weights; the maximum over all 12 microbatches (trajectory drift included) gets twice that
justification.gross_bounds: not accuracy limits: a no-op update gives norm ratio 0, a sign error cosine -1, a random/stale update cosine ~0, a missing or doubled normalisation scales m by 4 and v by 16; Adam's first steps are ~lr*sign(g), so a 25 % sign-flip rate would already lower the update cosine to ~0.5
justification.sampled_adamw: the per-base-call sampled AdamW ULP criterion (unchanged) checks optimizer arithmetic inside each run; it is not a whole-model gradient tolerance
